{"id": "f3f24dde-f47d-466b-984b-35ccd3218553", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_sDtnuh1rx2iyWi8GSxM1E0", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Understanding Consolidated Bills\",\"context\":\"### Calculating Costs for Amazon S3 Standard Storage\\n\\nThe following table shows an example of pricing tiers (your costs might vary). For\\nmore information, see Amazon S3 pricing.\\n\\n**Amazon S3 Pricing Tiers**\\n\\n| Tier description | Price per GB | Price per TB |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| First 1 TB/month | $0.10 | $100.00 |\\n| Next 49 TB/month | $0.08 | $80.00 |\\n| Next 450 TB/month | $0.06 | $60 |\\n\\nThe following table shows Amazon S3 usage for an organization that includes a management account and three member accounts.\\n\\n**Example S3 Usage Blended Cost**\\n\\n| Account | Tier | Storage amount (GB) | Storage amount (TB) | Unblended rate (/GB) | Unblended rate (/TB) | Unblended cost |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| Management | First TB/month | 1,000 | 1 | $0.10 | 100 | $100.00 |\\n| Next 49 TB/month | 49,000 | 49 | $0.08 | 80 | $3,920.00 |\\n| Next 450 TB/month | 45,000 | 45 | $0.06 | 60 | $2,700.00 |\\n| **Total** | | **95,000** | **95** | | | **$6,720.00** |\\n\\n| Account | Tier | Storage amount (GB) | Storage amount (TB) | Unblended rate (/GB) | Unblended rate (/TB) | Unblended cost | Blended rate (/GB) (=$6,720/95,000) | Blended rate (/TB) (=$6,720/95) | Blended cost (= Blended rate * storage) |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| Member 1 | First TB/month | 1,000 | 1 | $0.10 | 100 | $100.00 | 0.070737 | 70.737 | $70.37 |\\n| Next 49 TB/month | 14,000 | 14 | $0.08 | 80 | $1,120.00 | 0.070737\\n\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/con-bill-blended-rates.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"AWS Billing reports for Amazon S3\",\"context\":\"# AWS Billing reports for Amazon S3\\n\\nYour monthly bill from AWS separates your usage information and cost by AWS service and\\nfunction. There are several AWS Billing reports available: the monthly report, the\\ncost allocation report, and detailed billing reports. For information about how to see\\nyour billing reports, see Viewing\\nYour Bill in the *AWS Billing User Guide*.\\n\\nTo track your AWS usage and provide estimated charges associated with your account, you\\ncan set up AWS Cost and Usage Reports. For more information, see What are AWSCost and Usage Reports? in the *AWS Data\\nExports Guide*.\\n\\nYou can also download a usage report that gives more detail about your Amazon S3 storage\\nusage than the billing reports. For more information, see AWS usage reports for Amazon S3.\\n\\nThe following table lists the charges associated with Amazon S3 usage.\\n\\n| Charge | Comments |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| Storage | You pay for storing objects in your S3 buckets. The rate you're charged depends on your objects' size, how long you stored the objects during the month, and the storage class. Amazon S3 offers the following storage classes: S3 Standard, S3 Express One Zone, S3 Intelligent-Tiering, S3 Standard-IA (IA for infrequent access), S3 One Zone-IA, S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval, S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, S3 Glacier Deep Archive, or Reduced Redundancy Storage (RRS). For more information about storage classes, see Understanding and managing Amazon S3 storage classes. Be aware that if you have S3 Versioning enabled, you're charged for each version of an object that is retained. For more information about versioning, see How S3 Versioning works. |\\n| General purpose buckets | You're not billed for the first 2000 general purpose buckets that you create in your account. However, there is a per-bucket rate for each bucket that you create beyond the first 2000. This rate is billed per bucket/month. For information about general purpose bucket pricing, see Amazon S3 Pricing. |\\n| Monitoring and automation | You pay a monthly monitoring and automation fee per object stored in the S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class to monitor access patterns and move objects between access tiers in S3 Intelligent-Tiering. |\\n| Requests | You pay for requests, for example, `GET` requests, made against your S3 buckets and objects. This\\n\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/aws-billing-reports.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Understanding and managing Amazon S3 storage classes\",\"context\":\"## Comparing the Amazon S3 storage classes\\n\\nThe following table compares the storage classes, including their availability,\\ndurability, minimum storage duration, and other considerations.\\n\\n| Storage class | Designed for | Durability (designed for) | Availability (designed for) | Availability Zones | Min storage duration | Min billable object size | Other considerations |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| S3 Standard (`STANDARD`) | Frequently accessed data (more than once a month) with millisecond access | 99.999999999% | 99.99% | >= 3 | None | None | None |\\n| S3 Standard-IA (`STANDARD_IA`) | Long-lived, infrequently accessed data (once a month) with millisecond access | 99.999999999% | 99.9% | >= 3 | 30 days | 128 KB | Per-GB retrieval fees apply. |\\n| S3 Intelligent-Tiering (`INTELLIGENT_TIERING`) | Data with unknown, changing, or unpredictable access patterns | 99.999999999% | 99.9% | >= 3 | None | None | Monitoring and automation fees per object apply. No retrieval fees. Objects less than 128KB are not monitored and always stored in the Frequent Access tier. For more information, see How S3 Intelligent-Tiering works. |\\n| S3 One Zone-IA (`ONEZONE_IA`) | Recreatable, infrequently accessed data (once a month) with millisecond access | 99.999999999% | 99.5% | 1 | 30 days | 128 KB | Per-GB retrieval fees apply. Not resilient to the loss of the Availability Zone. |\\n| S3 Express One Zone (`EXPRESS_ONEZONE`) | Single-digit millisecond data access for latency-sensitive applications within a single AWS Availability Zone | 99.999999999% | 99.95% | 1 | None | None | S3 Express One Zone (`EXPRESS_ONEZONE`) objects are stored in a single AWS Availability Zone that you choose. |\\n| S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval (`GLACIER_IR`) | Long-lived, archive data accessed once a quarter with millisecond access | 99.999999999% | 99.9% | >= 3 | 90 days | 128 KB |\\n\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Look up current S3 Standard storage pricing for us-east-1 in AWS docs."}

{"id": "bb250ee0-5c8c-4862-ab60-d140188d8248", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's the S3 Standard storage pricing for **us-east-1** (as an example tiered structure — check the live AWS S3 pricing page for exact current rates, since these can change):

| Tier | Price per GB |
|---|---|
| First 1 TB/month | $0.10 |
| Next 49 TB/month | $0.08 |
| Next 450 TB/month | $0.06 |

A few other things that factor into your total S3 bill:
- **Requests**: charged per GET/PUT/other request type
- **Data transfer**: outbound transfer to the internet is billed (transfer within the same region is generally free)
- **Buckets**: the first 2,000 general-purpose buckets per account are free; a per-bucket monthly rate applies beyond that
- **Versioning**: if enabled, you're billed for every retained version of an object, not just the latest

Want me to break down an estimate for a specific storage volume or usage pattern?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
